title: Linkability of Location and Activity Data
description: GPS position data combined with timestamps and heart rate patterns can be linked across time periods to create a detailed profile of the user's movements, routines, and behaviors, potentially revealing sensitive information about their daily life.

title: Direct Identification Through Location Tracking
description: Continuous GPS telemetry can directly identify the user's home, workplace, and frequent locations, enabling identification of the individual even without explicit identifiers.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health and Location Data
description: Sensor telemetry including heart rate, GPS position, and timestamps may be transmitted or stored insecurely, leading to unauthorized access by third parties.

title: Excessive Data Collection Beyond Necessity
description: Continuous monitoring of heart rate, step counts, GPS, and timestamps may collect more personal data than necessary for the intended function, violating data minimization principles.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Privacy Laws
description: Continuous collection and processing of sensitive health and location data may violate GDPR, HIPAA, or other privacy regulations requiring explicit consent, data protection measures, and user rights.

title: Linkability of health data across contexts
description: Calorie, meal, and weight data logged by the user could be linked to their identity across different systems or time periods, potentially revealing patterns about their lifestyle, health status, or daily routines.

title: Identification of user from health data
description: The combination of weight entries, meal logs, and calorie intake data could potentially be used to identify the specific user, especially if this data is shared or accessed by third parties.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of personal health data
description: Sensitive health-related data (weight, meals, calories) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through app vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper sharing mechanisms.

title: Usurpation of user identity for data logging
description: An unauthorized person with access to the companion mobile app could impersonate the user and log false calorie, meal, or weight entries, compromising data integrity and privacy.

title: Excessive data collection beyond necessity
description: The app may collect more detailed health data (specific meals, exact calorie counts) than necessary for the stated purpose, potentially violating data minimization principles.

title: Linkability of Health Logs to Individuals
description: Health logs (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) written by the app can be linked to specific individuals through their app account, enabling profiling and tracking of personal health behaviors over time.
assumptions: App maintains persistent user accounts and logs are associated with user identities

title: Identifiability of Health Data Subjects
description: Health logs contain personally identifiable information that could be used to identify specific users, especially when combined with exercise session data and weight history patterns.
assumptions: Health data is inherently personal and can be correlated with user identity

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Logs
description: Health logs stored in the health log store could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, improper access controls, or insider threats.
assumptions: Data store may have vulnerabilities or insufficient access controls

title: Modification of Health Log Data
description: Health logs could be tampered with, altered, or deleted by unauthorized actors who gain access to the health log store, compromising data integrity and user trust.
assumptions: Data store may lack adequate integrity controls and audit mechanisms

title: Usurpation of User Identity for Health Data Access
description: Unauthorized users could potentially impersonate legitimate users to access their health logs through weak authentication mechanisms or credential theft.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to credential compromise

title: Non-compliance with Health Data Privacy Regulations
description: Collection and storage of health logs may violate privacy regulations such as GDPR, HIPAA, or other health data protection laws if proper consent, data minimization, and security measures are not implemented.
assumptions: Health data is classified as sensitive personal data under applicable regulations

title: Linkability of Location Traces
description: GPS location traces with timestamps can be linked across time periods to reconstruct detailed movement patterns, potentially revealing routines, habits, and associations between different locations.
assumptions: Location data is stored in a format that allows temporal correlation and pattern analysis.

title: Inference of Sensitive Information
description: Location history can be analyzed to infer sensitive information such as home address, workplace, religious sites, medical facilities, or political activities based on visit patterns and timing.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity and temporal detail to enable inference attacks.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location Data
description: Location history store may be accessed by unauthorized individuals or systems, exposing users' movement patterns and potentially enabling stalking, harassment, or physical security risks.
assumptions: Location history store has inadequate access controls or authentication mechanisms.

title: Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Location data may be shared with third parties such as advertisers, data brokers, or government agencies without user consent, leading to privacy violations and potential misuse of personal information.
assumptions: Data sharing agreements or policies allow third-party access to location data.

title: Usurpation of User Identity
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the user and access or modify their location history, leading to false location claims or unauthorized data manipulation.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak or compromised, allowing identity spoofing.

title: Health Log Data Identifiability Risk
description: The Health Analytics Service processes calorie, weight, and exercise logs that contain personally identifiable health information. Even with anonymization attempts, the combination of health metrics across multiple sessions could enable re-identification of individuals through pattern matching or cross-referencing with other data sources.
assumptions: The analytics service has access to complete historical health data across sessions, and there may be insufficient de-identification measures in place.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is a reasonable fit for identifiability threats in health data processing, but exact LINDDUN Pro node numbering may vary.

title: Unauthorized Health Data Disclosure
description: The Health Analytics Service may inadvertently or maliciously disclose sensitive health information to unauthorized parties. This could occur through improper access controls, data leakage during processing, or insufficient encryption of data in transit or at rest.
assumptions: The analytics service may have inadequate access controls or encryption mechanisms protecting health data during processing.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 represents disclosure threats, which is appropriate for unauthorized data exposure scenarios.

title: Health Data Linkability Across Sessions
description: Multiple sessions of health log data (calorie, weight, exercise) can be linked together to create a comprehensive health profile of an individual. This linkability enables tracking of health trends and behaviors over time, potentially revealing sensitive health conditions or lifestyle patterns.
assumptions: The analytics service processes data across multiple sessions without sufficient measures to prevent linking of individual records.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 addresses linkability concerns, which is relevant for multi-session health data aggregation.

title: Health Data Manipulation Risk
description: The Health Analytics Service could have the opportunity to alter, modify, or tamper with health log data during processing. This could affect the accuracy of health-condition analysis and potentially lead to incorrect medical insights or recommendations.
assumptions: The analytics service has write access or modification capabilities to the health data it processes.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 represents data manipulation threats, applicable when data integrity is at risk during processing.

title: Health Data Processing Compliance Risk
description: The Health Analytics Service may fail to comply with health data protection regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) when processing sensitive health information. This could result in legal penalties, loss of trust, and regulatory violations.
assumptions: The analytics service may not have proper compliance frameworks or may process data in ways that violate health data protection laws.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nc.1.1 addresses non-compliance threats, which is relevant for regulated health data processing.

title: Location History Linkability
description: Location history data from DS2 can be linked to specific individuals across multiple sessions, enabling tracking of individual movements and associations with other data sources.
assumptions: Data is not properly anonymized or pseudonymized before storage or transmission.

title: Movement Pattern Identification
description: Daily routine and movement patterns derived from location history can be used to identify individuals even without explicit identifiers, revealing personal habits and locations.
assumptions: Pattern analysis algorithms can extract identifying information from aggregated movement data.

title: Unauthorized Location Data Disclosure
description: Location history data accessed by the Health Analytics Service may be disclosed to unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, improper access controls, or data breaches.
assumptions: Access controls are not properly implemented or enforced.

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: Collecting location history across all sessions may exceed what is necessary for deriving daily routine patterns, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: The analytics service collects more granular location data than required for its stated purpose.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Processing of location history data may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA) due to the sensitive nature of location data and lack of proper consent mechanisms.
assumptions: Location data is classified as sensitive personal data under applicable regulations.

title: Linkability of Health Analytics Data
description: Inferred health insights (risk indicators, routine summaries, trend flags) sent from Health Analytics Service to Companion Mobile App could be linked with other data sources (e.g., medical records, insurance data, device usage patterns) to create comprehensive user profiles.
assumptions: Data is stored in multiple systems and accessible across platforms

title: Identifiability of Health Condition Indicators
description: Health-condition risk indicators and trend flags could potentially identify specific individuals, especially when combined with other available data (e.g., device identifiers, location data, usage patterns).
assumptions: Health data is unique enough to identify individuals when combined with other data points

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Analytics
description: Inferred health insights transmitted from Health Analytics Service could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through interception, system vulnerabilities, or improper access controls.
assumptions: Data transmission and storage may not have adequate security controls

title: Excessive Health Data Collection
description: Companion Mobile App may receive and store more detailed health analytics data than necessary for its intended functionality, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: App may cache or store analytics data beyond what is needed for display

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance for Health Data
description: Transmission of health-condition risk indicators and trend flags may violate healthcare privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) if proper consent, encryption, and access controls are not implemented.
assumptions: Health data is considered protected health information under applicable regulations

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health indicators
description: The app dashboard displays inferred condition indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) which are highly sensitive health data. If unauthorized access occurs to the app or data transmission is intercepted, this sensitive health information could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Health data is considered sensitive personal information under privacy regulations

title: Linkability of health data across systems
description: The health indicators displayed in the app could potentially be linked with other data sources (e.g., medical records, insurance data, or other apps) creating a comprehensive health profile of the user without consent.
assumptions: Data may be shared with third-party services or integrated with other health platforms

title: Identification of user through health patterns
description: The displayed trends and condition indicators could uniquely identify the user, especially if combined with other data, revealing sensitive health status that the user may wish to keep private.
assumptions: Health indicators are distinctive enough to identify individuals

title: Unauthorized access to app dashboard
description: The user (wearer) could potentially lose access to their own health dashboard, or unauthorized individuals could gain access to the app and view sensitive health information if authentication is compromised.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be vulnerable to attacks

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Health Data
description: Health and location datasets hosted at the cloud provider could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through insider threats, compromised access controls, or data breaches.

title: Data Tampering with Health Analytics
description: Analytics data and models could be tampered with by the cloud provider or attackers, compromising data integrity and potentially leading to incorrect health analytics results.

title: Data Misuse by Cloud Provider
description: The cloud hosting provider could misuse the health and location data for purposes beyond the agreed scope, such as selling data to third parties or using it for unauthorized profiling.

title: Re-identification of Individuals
description: The combination of health data and location data could enable re-identification of individuals, even if data is anonymized, due to the unique nature of health and location information.

title: Linkability of Health Data
description: Health data could be linked with other datasets (e.g., government records, commercial data) held by the cloud provider or third parties, creating comprehensive profiles of individuals.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violations
description: Hosting sensitive health data at a third-party cloud provider may violate GDPR, HIPAA, or other healthcare data protection regulations if proper safeguards and data processing agreements are not in place.
